Each page gives the holding first, then the question, why the case matters, how Congress responded, and the statutes at issue. Every case links to the official opinion: the bound *United States Reports* on GovInfo, or the Supreme Court's slip opinion for recent decisions.

| Case | Year | Holding | Statutes at issue |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Curtiss-Wright](curtiss-wright-1936.qmd) | 1936 | Upheld the delegation. Because foreign affairs powers rest on national sovereignty rather than on the Constitution's specific grants alone, Congress may give the President broader discretion abroad than at home. | [Constitution (war powers)](../statutes/constitution-war-powers.qmd) |
| [Youngstown](youngstown-1952.qmd) | 1952 | Held the seizure unlawful. No statute authorized it, and the President's powers as Commander in Chief and chief executive did not extend to taking private property at home to settle a labor dispute; that was lawmaking reserved to Congress. | [Constitution (war powers)](../statutes/constitution-war-powers.qmd), [Defense Production Act](../statutes/dpa-1950.qmd), [Selective Service Act](../statutes/selective-service-1948.qmd) |
| [Train v. New York](train-v-ny-1975.qmd) | 1975 | No. The statute required the Administrator to allot the full sums authorized; he had no discretion to withhold them. | [Impoundment Control Act](../statutes/impoundment-1974.qmd) |
| [Dames & Moore](dames-moore-1981.qmd) | 1981 | Yes. IEEPA authorized nullifying the attachments and transferring the assets. No statute expressly authorized suspending the claims, but Congress's long acquiescence in executive settlement of international claims, and related statutes, supported the President's action. | [IEEPA](../statutes/ieepa-1977.qmd) |
| [INS v. Chadha](chadha-1983.qmd) | 1983 | No. Action with the effect of law must pass both houses and be presented to the President. | [War Powers Resolution](../statutes/wpr-1973.qmd), [National Emergencies Act](../statutes/nea-1976.qmd), [Arms Export Control Act](../statutes/aeca-1976.qmd) |
| [Hamdi](hamdi-2004.qmd) | 2004 | The 2001 AUMF authorizes detaining individuals who fought against the United States in Afghanistan as part of or supporting Taliban forces, including citizens, for the duration of the relevant hostilities. | [2001 AUMF](../statutes/aumf-2001.qmd) |
| [Hamdan](hamdan-2006.qmd) | 2006 | No. The commissions' procedures violated the Uniform Code of Military Justice, which requires that commission rules match those of courts-martial as far as practicable, and Common Article 3 of the Geneva Conventions. | [UCMJ](../statutes/ucmj-1950.qmd), [Detainee Treatment Act](../statutes/dta-2005.qmd) |
| [Boumediene](boumediene-2008.qmd) | 2008 | Yes, they have the privilege. Sec. 7 of the Military Commissions Act, which stripped federal courts of jurisdiction over their habeas petitions, operates as an unconstitutional suspension of the writ, and the review procedures of the Detainee Treatment Act are not an adequate substitute. | [Military Commissions Act](../statutes/mil-commissions-2006.qmd), [Detainee Treatment Act](../statutes/dta-2005.qmd) |
| [Humanitarian Law Project](hlp-2010.qmd) | 2010 | Yes, as applied to the plaintiffs' proposed activities. The ban in 18 U.S.C. 2339B is not unconstitutionally vague and does not violate the First Amendment, given Congress's and the executive's judgment that any support frees resources for terrorism. | [AEDPA (terrorism)](../statutes/aedpa-1996.qmd) |
| [Clapper v. Amnesty](clapper-2013.qmd) | 2013 | No. Their fear that their communications would be collected was too speculative to establish the concrete, imminent injury Article III requires, and their costs to avoid surveillance could not substitute for it. | [FISA Amendments Act (702)](../statutes/fisa-amendments-2008.qmd) |
| [Zivotofsky v. Kerry](zivotofsky-2015.qmd) | 2015 | No. The power to recognize foreign states and governments belongs to the President alone, and Sec. 214(d) of the Foreign Relations Authorization Act, Fiscal Year 2003, which required the listing, unconstitutionally infringed it. | [Constitution (war powers)](../statutes/constitution-war-powers.qmd) |
| [Learning Resources v. Trump](learning-resources-2026.qmd) | 2026 | No. IEEPA does not authorize the President to impose tariffs. The Court affirmed the Federal Circuit's judgment against the tariffs in the companion case and ordered the challenge brought in district court dismissed for lack of jurisdiction. | [IEEPA](../statutes/ieepa-1977.qmd) |
